neet_phy_u10_t09_1.working: The phase difference is π/2, so the amplitudes add in quadrature: A = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 mm.

neet_phy_u10_t09_3.working: Adding the waves: a[sin(kx−ωt) + sin(kx+ωt)] = 2a sin kx cos ωt. At x = 0, sin kx = 0, so x = 0 is a node.

neet_phy_u10_t09_4.working: Resultant amplitude is R = 2a cos(φ/2). φ = 0 gives 2a (III); φ = π gives 0 (II); φ = π/2 gives √2a (IV); φ = 2π/3 gives a (I).

neet_phy_u10_t09_5.working: A is true: rigid-boundary reflection gives a phase change of π. B is false: a pulse is not inverted at a free end. C is true: frequency is unchanged on reflection. D is true: waves pass through each other unaffected. E is false: destructive interference gives |a1 − a2|. So A, C, D are correct.
